newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - May 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - May 9.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The last phase of the Comprehensive Tax Reform Package increasing individual tax exemptions by almost 200 percent was approved yesterday on third reading by the House of Representatives. (TIMES/BULLETIN/STAR)

- The Philippine Central Bank recommended on Thursday the investigation of 16 former officials of Monte de Piedad and Savings Bank who could be liable for the bank's failed lending programme that resulted in 1.8 billion pesos in losses. (TODAY/STAR/CHORNICLE)

- Manila allowed three Chinese vessels to pass through Philippine waters en route to the Marshall Islands after Beijing complied with requirements, sources from the Department of Foreign Affairs said on Thursday. (INQUIRER)
- The Philippines will waive the use of any additional sugar quota allocation that the United States government may grant in the fourth quarter of quota year 1996-97. (STANDARD/BUSINESS DAILY))
- The Philippine Central Bank lowered its overnight borrowing rate to 11.25 from 11.50 percent ON Thursday, but raised its overnight lending rate to 13 from 12.65 percent. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- The Securities and Exchange Commission is set to issue an order suspending or revoking the license of stockbrokers who trade in securities using their own personal accounts. (BUSINESS DAILY/BUSINESSWORLD)
